title: Materialize one bounded prompt, preflight it, then execute the exact same artifact
purpose: Prevent clipboard mutation or operator re-copy from changing the sprint between AgentSwitchboard preflight and execution.
triggers: OpenCode sprint prompt starts on the Windows clipboard
PlanOnly or preflight is requested before a bounded sprint
operator would otherwise need to copy the prompt a second time
preflight and execution must prove prompt identity continuity
inputs: prompt path or one clipboard snapshot
steps: Resolve the target repository and existing OpenCode launcher without mutating product code.
Read the prompt exactly once from the supplied file or clipboard intake source.
Materialize those exact prompt bytes to a run-local untracked bounded-sprint-prompt.md artifact.
Compute and record SHA-256 and character count without copying raw prompt text into the receipt or report.
Invoke the existing OpenCode launcher in PlanOnly mode with -PromptPath pointing to the materialized artifact.
Stop immediately if preflight exits nonzero; preserve the artifact and receipt for recovery.
Recompute SHA-256 after preflight and fail closed if the prompt artifact changed.
Unless PreflightOnly was explicitly requested, invoke the existing OpenCode launcher again with the exact same -PromptPath and bounds.
Record execute exit code and final digest, and fail closed if prompt identity changed or execution failed.
Write the machine-readable receipt and human operator report outside the repository.
failureHandling: Never ask the operator to copy the prompt again merely to continue the same run.
Never silently fall back to the current clipboard after a prompt artifact has been materialized.
Never delete the run-local prompt automatically after a failed preflight or execution; it is recovery evidence.
Route launcher/product defects to the product owner; this harness lane may not patch product code.
outputs: OpenCode/GNHF downstream evidence paths printed by the delegated launcher
proofCeiling: Prompt transport and gate ordering only. A successful harness run does not itself prove provider response, code quality, branch push, PR state, merge, deployment, or end-user acceptance.
